column1: # The byte ranges are computed from the FROZEN source at C1, from the
# C1-frozen digests, and are re-derived at C3 from the same digests.
# The ranges are UNIQUE in their files: the searched text appears
# exactly ONCE in the selector-ON region. The C3 phase RECOMPUTES the
# ranges and REJECTS a mutation whose range is not unique, so a
# mutation cannot silently hit a different statement.

column2: the four experiments touch DIFFERENT files or DIFFERENT unique ranges
no mutation lands in a semantic function outside the named one
after each experiment the source is restored and the restored bytes are VERIFIED against the frozen digest
after each experiment the rebuilt object is verified against the frozen digest
no two producers are the same executable
each generation is produced by a DISTINCT producer executable

column1: # SECTION 4 -- THE FOUR-GENERATION PRODUCER DAG PLAN
# G0 is the pure C-driver oracle, built with the selector OFF. G1, G2
# and G3 are the SAME PolyC driver source compiled by THREE DISTINCT
# PRODUCER EXECUTABLES, distinguished by content SHA-256.
# A producer is an EXECUTABLE; an object is a FILE. Two producers may
# legitimately produce byte-identical objects, because they are the
# same compiler generation. That is MEASURED, not assumed.

column2: an independently built qualified bootstrap generation

column2: the symbol table carries ZERO _WpDriver symbols
the relocations carry ZERO references to the driver subject
the binary carries NO trace of the new status-domain member's decision path
the observable behaviour on the frozen fixtures is the LEGACY behaviour

column1: # The "no trace of the new status member" check is the one the
# correction could break: the new member lives in the PolyC driver,
# which the G0 oracle does not link, so the oracle must carry NO
# trace of it. The check is MECHANICAL: the G0 binary's symbol table
# and relocations must carry zero driver references, and the G0
# binary's behaviour on FX_PREC_STDOUT_BAD must be the LEGACY one.
